title: Metering Service Billing Note: Demand Charges in a Referee Refund Settlement
content:
A **Metering Service** referee refund settlement on an Electric Service Agreement billed on a schedule with a demand charge reprices demand charges according to the billing demand of the repriced bills.

| The schedule carries a demand charge | A repriced bill was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand | Charges repriced |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | At least one | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every repriced bill, plus the demand charges of the repriced bills billed above the minimum |
| Yes | None | Energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every repriced bill |
| No | (not applicable) | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; no demand charge |

**Formal statement.** Where the service agreement's rate schedule carries a demand charge and at least one bill the referee refund settlement reprices was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every repriced bill plus the demand charges of the repriced bills billed above that minimum. Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no repriced bill was billed at the minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every repriced bill.

**Billed at the minimum** means the bill's billing demand in kW equals the schedule's minimum billing demand.

**Hypothetical pair.** Five repriced bills on a schedule with a 75 kW minimum, of which one shows 75 kW: the demand charges of the other four are repriced. If that bill had shown 76 kW, the demand charges of all five would be repriced.
